caption:
Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5 on 24 July. The headline is not that it is better. It is that the price did not move.

$5 per million input tokens, $25 per million output tokens — exactly what Opus 4.8 cost. And on ARC-AGI 3, an evaluation where the model has to solve novel problems, Anthropic reports Opus 5 scoring three times as high as the next-best model.

Two caveats we are not going to bury. Almost every figure in that launch post is Anthropic's own, and its footnote says the headline coding result came from an internal run, mean reward over 5 attempts per task. The one check here that is not Anthropic's — Simon Willison finding Opus 5 on top of the third-party Artificial Analysis leaderboard on launch day — is a snapshot of a leaderboard that moves.

Sources on every slide.
Primary: anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5
Corroboration: simonwillison.net, techcrunch.com

slides.headline: Claude Opus 5: same price as 4.8, *three times* the next best on ARC-AGI

slides.title: The price *did not move*
slides.body: Opus 5 launched at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens. That is exactly what Opus 4.8 cost — the model it replaces.
slides.evidence: Claude Opus 5 is available today on all platforms, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens (the same as Opus 4.8).

slides.title: *Three times* the next best
slides.body: ARC-AGI 3 is an evaluation where the model has to solve novel problems. On it, Anthropic reports Opus 5 scoring three times as high as the next-best model.
slides.evidence: On ARC-AGI 3 , an evaluation where the model has to solve novel problems, Opus 5's score is three times as high as the next-best model.

slides.title: Source code yes, *binaries no*
slides.body: Opus 5 is permitted to search source code for vulnerabilities, but its safeguards stop it scanning a compiled binary for them — the source-code task being the one more likely to be defensive.
slides.evidence: For instance, Opus 5 safeguards prevent it from being used to scan for vulnerabilities in a software binary, although it is permitted to search for vulnerabilities in source code, since the latter task is more likely to be used for defensive purposes.

slides.title: Now the *independent* check
slides.body: None of the above is independent. So: on launch day Simon Willison checked the third-party Artificial Analysis leaderboard, and found Opus 5 leading it — in front of even Fable 5.
slides.evidence: It's currently leading the Artificial Analysis leaderboard , in front of even Fable 5.

slides.title: Read the *footnotes*
slides.body: Anthropic's headline coding result comes from an internal run, mean reward over 5 attempts per task. That is a claim by the company selling the model, not an independent measurement.
slides.evidence: These results are from an internal run of Frontier-Bench v0.1, on the mini-swe-agent harness and a GKE backend, mean reward over 5 attempts per task.

slides.headline: Follow for *one verified story* a day
slides.sub: No hype. No reposts. Sources on every slide.
